Explicar qué está confirmado, qué difiere y qué debe verificarse.

teaching.en: The bulletin headline “West entrance reopens” and the audio headline “Friday market access” are shorter than their leads. Both sources report a Friday reopening and a queue sign. The bulletin says two card readers work; the shopkeeper says only one works, so the count is uncertain. Neither source confirms the repair cause. A factual summary must attribute those details, compare the disagreement and verify it with the market office instead of inventing a reason. The two short headlines orient the reader, while the attributed leads supply the facts that the final comparison summarizes and checks carefully.

answer.text: “River path reopens” is the website headline, while “Tuesday river update” is the radio headline; each lead supplies the details. Both attributed reports agree on Tuesday and the north-gate sign. They disagree because the website gives two entrances and radio gives only one. The cause is not confirmed, so it must remain uncertain. I would check the council’s current entrance map and contact the path office. This comparison keeps headline and lead separate, summarizes the common facts, identifies the conflict and proposes verification without adding unsupported information. The verified details remain clear.

The website headline, “River path reopens,” and the radio headline, “Tuesday river update,” are shorter than their leads. Both sources confirm a Tuesday reopening and a new sign at the north gate. The website reports two entrances, while radio says the north gate is the only entrance, so the count remains uncertain. Neither confirms a cause. I would compare the current council map with the radio report and ask the path office to verify the entrances. This source-based summary separates headlines, attributed facts, uncertainty, agreement and disagreement without inventing a reason for every reader.

feedback.es: The two visible sources provide overlap, conflict and a cautious verification step.

origin.text: Source A — Town website. Headline: River path reopens. Lead: The council reported that the path reopened on Tuesday, with a new sign at the north gate and two entrances. Source B — local radio. Headline: Tuesday river update. Lead: The presenter said the path reopened on Tuesday and mentioned the new sign, but said the north gate was the only entrance. Neither source confirms why the path reopened.

feedback.es: Both sources give the same reopening day and entrance.

“Library adds evening hours” and “Monday library update” are the two short headlines; their leads contain the evidence. The school notice and student radio agree on Monday hours, a quiet-study room and a new booking form. They disagree on capacity: the notice reports twenty desks, while radio reports eighteen. Neither source confirms who changed the hours, so that point remains uncertain. I would check the current library notice and ask the librarian to verify the desk count. This summary attributes each fact, distinguishes headlines from details and records the disagreement without inventing a responsible person before publication.

feedback.es: The school sources give two coincidences, one capacity conflict and a verification action.

Source B — student radio. Headline: Monday library update. Lead: The presenter reported the same hours and booking form, but said the room has eighteen desks. Neither source confirms who changed the hours.
